threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still wait for the bus even when the Tube's down, not realizing the 38 is quicker. Everyone knows 'overground' is not just a train line but a lifestyle.
Caught a lad on the 59 last night, loudly boasting about his 'secret' karaoke spot in Clapham. Can't say I was impressed, but the bus drivers were all in on it.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I realized I was really home when I saw the spontaneous dance party on the street during the bus strike—everyone laughing, helping each other out with rides.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you grab a currywurst at 3 AM and watch street artists transform a post-war building into a canvas overnight.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only a local knows not to panic when the BART goes down; we just hop on the nearest taco truck and wait it out like it’s part of our commute.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy serenading Muni riders with a ukulele at Civic Center, totally oblivious to the chaos around him. Just another day in the TL.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists miss that the real pa amb tomàquet is made with raw, dried bread, not toasted. You can spot locals’ disdain when they see the soggy versions served everywhere.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their overuse of 'gràcies' even when ordering a simple café. Locals skip the pleasantries to save time.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the Tube' when you’re in the bus lane, blissfully unaware that key trains aren’t included in your Oyster card.
Heard a guy on the 159 last night debating the merits of Jerk chicken vs Fried chicken with a complete stranger. Best part? They ended up sharing a portion!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home the day I saw a group of kids getting off the bus, all wearing matching tracksuits, and they immediately fought over who could sit on the back seat.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain do you find a bar that serves cocktails in old glass beakers, tapping into that quirky scientist vibe. Never seen it anywhere else.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they casually mention the 'dog on the tracks' incident like it’s just another Tuesday in the city.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 47 today, and a guy in a full tuxedo was practicing his dance moves in the aisle. Unphased Muni riders just kept scrolling their phones.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just Gaudí and hipster cafes, but it’s really about the small, family-run talleres and nightly jam sessions in the plazas.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they stand in line for a café, too polite to jump ahead like locals do, sipping their coffee with that puzzled look.
